answer: A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The relic multiplier is published, charged in harbor, and dune lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 12 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 3017 identities would post 3248 proofs and burn roughly 10 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
